diff --git a/hooks/grade-recall.py b/hooks/grade-recall.py
index ef84cb57..9c3aa6fc 100755
--- a/hooks/grade-recall.py
+++ b/hooks/grade-recall.py
@@ -839,6 +839,16 @@ def main():
         "reports admitted-are-gold precision + gold coverage; exit 1 on kill",
     )
     a = ap.parse_args()
+    if CHITTA_EVAL_SOCKET:
+        # A dead replica must abort, not score 0.0 (happened 2026-09-13 when the
+        # replica refused to start mid-save and the grader ran anyway).
+        probe = subprocess.run(
+            _chitta_cli("recall", "--query", "ping", "--limit", "1"),
+            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60,
+        )
+        if probe.returncode != 0 or "Cannot connect" in (probe.stdout + probe.stderr):
+            print(f"eval replica at {CHITTA_EVAL_SOCKET} is not reachable; aborting", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
     if a.no_reranker:
         global _reranker
         _reranker = False
@@ -1083,4 +1093,4 @@ def main():
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
-    main()
+    sys.exit(main())

reasons: Touches hooks/grade-recall.py, which computes eval/grading metrics (admitted-are-gold precision, gold coverage); it does not touch a separate gold/hidden/ledger data file, only the grading harness's own control flow.

No reward inflation: the change makes the grader stricter, not looser — it now aborts (exit 2) rather than silently scoring 0.0 when the eval replica socket is unreachable, so it removes a failure mode that previously produced a misleadingly low (not inflated) score; net effect is toward more honest measurement, not Goodharting upward.
No frozen-contract artifacts (RPC shapes, '#<id> [pct%]' lines, snapshot/WAL formats) appear in this diff at all — only a CLI probe subprocess call and a return-code check are added.

Blast radius: change is confined to grade-recall.py's main(), gated behind CHITTA_EVAL_SOCKET being set, so it only affects eval-replica runs, not the live production daemon/hooks path; the sys.exit(main()) change ensures the new exit code 2 actually propagates as a process exit status, which is a behavior change for any caller relying on exit codes but is disclosed via the comment and is low-risk/reversible (revert is a two-line diff).

No pre-registered bet or verdict is present in this diff; the added comment references a past 2026-09-13 incident as motivation but supplies no bet/threshold/evidence structure, so the bet-resolution rubric item has nothing to evaluate — this is a gap rather than a violation, so it does not by itself justify a block.
